$description: The DTCG single-source design tokens (UI-Architecture §3, D42). Values seed from the design handoff's Hearth OKLCH ramp + Ember accent + Geist (UI-Architecture §4.1 — ONLY the palette survives the seed). Everything downstream (src/styles/theme.css @theme block + src/tokens/index.ts typed map) is DERIVED by tokens.build.ts — never hand-authored.

background.$description: near-neutral charcoal (chroma ~0.006 @ hue 60) so the ONE Ember reads as intentional — UIP-101

surface-raised.$description: the elevation-RAMP mid panel tone (D44 §12.1 appearance.elevation=ramp) — a perceptible step between --color-sidebar (0.132, rail) and --color-card (0.205), so LIST/CONTEXT panels lift off the rail. Unused by the default flat composition; consumed only by shell.css `.shell-grid[data-elevation=ramp]`.

popover-foreground.$description: ONE white. It was a hand-authored oklch(0.96 0.004 75) — 0.005 lighter than --color-foreground for no stated reason, which rendered as two near-identical whites on one surface (a Select's popup value vs the labels beside it; preset typography census, 2026-08-02). The token stays SEMANTIC (a theme may still retint text-on-popover); only the unjustified drift in the base ramp goes.

primary.$description: Ember — the ONE signature accent (richer, glowing — UIP-101)

secondary.$description: ONE low-emphasis neutral surface — the same de-drift as popover-foreground/accent-foreground. It was a hand-authored oklch(0.255 0.007 60) against muted's oklch(0.255 0.006 60): identical lightness and hue, 0.001 chroma apart (Oklab ΔE 0.0010), i.e. the same colour spelled twice (near-duplicate lint, 2026-08-02). muted holds the literal because it is the more-consumed of the two (83 utility sites vs 35), so the collapse moves the fewest pixels. The token stays SEMANTIC — every seed value-set re-values secondary and muted independently, and a theme may still separate them.

muted-foreground.$description: secondary/placeholder text — AA on every Hearth surface incl. the input fill (worst ≈4.9:1 over input-on-popover; the prior 0.705 was 4.29:1 there — a marginal AA miss). Custom themes derive this via theme-scope/clamp mutedForegroundOn.

accent-foreground.$description: ONE white — the same de-drift as popover-foreground above (was oklch(0.96 0.004 75); a selected/highlighted row's text must not be a second white beside the unselected rows it sits with).

destructive.$description: POLARITY-AWARE via CSS light-dark() (arg order is light-arm FIRST, dark-arm second): ONE static semantic token with two hand-tuned arms selected by the inherited color-scheme (base :root dark, [data-theme=light] flips to light). A single static red physically cannot clear AA-NORMAL 4.5:1 as text on BOTH a near-black chrome and a near-white card — so the dark arm (oklch(0.72 0.19 25)) is a bright red that clears on dark surfaces (6.42:1 card, 5.82:1 popover) and the light arm (oklch(0.50 0.19 25)) is a deeper red that clears on the light seed's card/popover at 6.54:1. Paired with the destructive-foreground below it also clears AA-NORMAL as a solid `bg-destructive` pill in each polarity (dark 6.53:1, light 6.24:1). THE DARK ARM JOINED THE FAMILY BAND (2026-09-01, was oklch(0.65 0.19 25) at 5.07:1 card / 4.59:1 popover): 0.65 left it the ONLY dark accent below the band its siblings occupy (success 0.72, primary 0.72, info 0.70), and a token at the family FLOOR has nothing to spend — it was the one ink that failed on every ground quieter than the card, including the `bg-accent` a ListRow/Card paints on hover (4.07:1 hearth / 3.98:1 mocha bare, 3.72:1 / 3.68:1 under the soft chip's own tint), which is exactly the composition nobody had priced. At 0.72 every one of those pairs clears with margin and the pill improves 5.15:1 -> 6.53:1; the light arm and the hue/chroma are untouched, so this is the same red, at the lightness the rest of the family already uses. The bright/dark-foreground convention matches the rest of the accent family.

destructive-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): text on the solid `bg-destructive` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.2 0.03 25), the original) is DARK text on the bright dark-scheme red (6.53:1 since the dark arm joined the family band, was 5.15:1); the light arm (oklch(0.98 0.01 25)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme red (6.24:1) — the light red is dark enough to take a light foreground, the opposite polarity from dark. Only ever sits on `bg-destructive`, never a neutral surface.

success.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): the success/confirm green. Dark arm (oklch(0.72 0.13 155), the original) clears AA as `text-success` on dark chrome; the light arm (oklch(0.47 0.12 155)) is a deeper green clearing 6.32:1 as text on the light seed's card, and 5.90:1 as a solid pill under the light success-foreground below.

success-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): text on the solid `bg-success` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.14 0.02 150), the original) is dark text on the bright dark-scheme green; the light arm (oklch(0.97 0.01 150)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme green (5.90:1).

warning.$description: the partial/caution intent (rpg check bands, staleness). POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): dark arm (oklch(0.79 0.13 75), the original) is the bright amber for dark chrome; the light arm (oklch(0.50 0.11 75)) is a deeper amber clearing 6.03:1 as text on the light seed's card, and 5.77:1 as a solid pill under the light warning-foreground below.

warning-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): text on the solid `bg-warning` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.2 0.03 85), the original) is dark text on the bright dark-scheme amber; the light arm (oklch(0.98 0.01 85)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme amber (5.77:1).

info.$description: informational intent (UIP-101 new token; mockup .theme-hearth --info). POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first): dark arm (oklch(0.7 0.1 232), the original W2 value) is the bright blue for dark chrome; the light arm (oklch(0.48 0.1 232)) is a deeper blue clearing 6.29:1 as text on the light seed's card. Paired with the info-foreground below it also clears AA-NORMAL as a solid `bg-info` pill in each polarity (north-star PP1 minted the foreground; per-palette pill-swept). Arms are written in browser-round-trip form (no trailing zeros) so the badge CT's `toHaveCSS(resolvedTokenColor)` matches the computed style — same color as W2's `0.70 0.10`.

info-foreground.$description: POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first; D71 static intent token, north-star PP1): text on the solid `bg-info` pill. Dark arm (oklch(0.2 0.03 232)) is dark text on the bright dark-scheme blue (6.90:1); the light arm (oklch(0.98 0.01 232)) is near-white text on the deeper light-scheme blue (6.03:1). Mirrors the success/warning foreground shape (bright bg → dark fg on dark scheme, deeper bg → near-white fg on light scheme). Only ever sits on `bg-info`, never a neutral surface.

highlight.$description: text-mark / search-match highlight — a bright, more-yellow highlighter tone, deliberately distinct from warning's caution amber. POLARITY-INDEPENDENT: unlike the 4 divergent intents (destructive/success/warning/info) this is ONE plain value, NOT a light-dark() pair — a saturated yellow mark reads on both a black and a white page, and highlight is a BACKGROUND, so the only AA constraint is the dark highlight-foreground on it (9.98:1). THE RULING SURVIVES; ITS INPUT CHANGED (2026-09-01): the clause used to read -never rendered as text-, and that premise was FALSE — three surfaces painted `text-highlight` (the rail crown, the rpg game-door kicker, the header band), where the light seed rendered this gold at 1.41-1.71:1, i.e. invisible. Text duty is not this token's job and never was: it now belongs to `color.accolade` below, the polarity-aware INK that references this gold for its dark arm and deepens on light. So the mark stays highlighter yellow in every polarity — background-only, as ruled — and the premise is now true by construction rather than by assumption. The former light-dark(X,X) was a literal no-op (both arms identical) that implied two tuned arms; collapsed to the single value it always resolved to.

highlight-foreground.$description: POLARITY-INDEPENDENT (a single plain value, mirroring highlight — not a light-dark() pair): dark text on the `bg-highlight` mark, 9.98:1. The highlight mark is the same saturated yellow on both pages, so the foreground stays the one dark tone; the former no-op light-dark(X,X) was collapsed.

accolade.$description: the DISTINCTION ink — gold TEXT/glyph marking a cell as the one that owns something (the context rail's crown on a host-only cell, the rpg game-door kicker, the header band's owning link). Named for the treatment, not for a surface or a domain: it lives in @orb/ui's neutral vocabulary and must stay speakable by any consumer. POLARITY-AWARE light-dark() (light arm first, in themes/light.json), and it REFERENCES color.highlight for its dark arm rather than re-spelling that gold — on a dark page the mark and the accolade ARE the same decision, and a re-spelled twin is the exact drift the near-duplicate lint exists to prevent. They diverge only on light, where a mark and an ink want opposite things: the mark must stay a saturated highlighter yellow BEHIND dark text, while an ink at that lightness is 1.41-1.71:1 against every light surface. The light arm (oklch(0.48 0.12 100)) sits in the same 0.47-0.50 band the four divergent intents use and clears AA-NORMAL on every light ground the three sites touch, worst case the rail's own active row: sidebar-accent 4.77:1, sidebar 5.63:1, card 6.34:1, background 6.07:1. Minted 2026-09-01 when the seed ink-duty audit measured the gold as text; before that the three sites wore `text-highlight` (see color.highlight above).

field-fill.$description: The FILL of a text-field box (input, textarea, select trigger, combobox). A separate token from --color-input, which also paints borderless rails and switch tracks that must stay translucent so they read against a card.

input-border.$description: THE FORM-CONTROL BORDER (D159; #1641 / #1361 item 1, owner ruling 2026-09-05) — the opaque, polarity-aware edge that IDENTIFIES an input, select trigger, textarea or input-group as a control. MINTED RATHER THAN RAISING `--color-border`: the shared border is `oklch(0.99 0.005 60 / 0.08)`, an 8%-alpha hairline with 72 consumers, and it measured 1.190–1.318:1 against every ground a form control sits on (Hearth 1.190 on `color.background`, 1.276 on the `bg-input` rail; Light 1.265–1.283; Mocha 1.193–1.318) — the 45 `border-contrast` findings on settings:chat-behavior, 5 on appearance, 8 on admin. WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 governs the boundary of a USER-INTERFACE COMPONENT, not a decorative divider, so taking all 72 consumers to 3:1 would have made every rule in the app shout to satisfy a floor that binds on a dozen. `--color-border` is unchanged and still owns non-form borders. IT IS OPAQUE ON PURPOSE, the `--color-selection-quiet` lesson: an alpha edge's real colour is whatever is behind it, so it cannot be measured once (`alpha-token-needs-composited-contrast-probe`). BOUNDED FROM BOTH SIDES. FLOOR: 1.4.11's 3:1 against every ground a control's edge meets — each chrome panel AND the `bg-input` fill composited over it, worst of the float and 8-bit-quantized ratio. The worst ground is the `bg-accent` an interactive row paints on hover, with the field fill over it: 3.257 (Hearth), 3.369 (Light), 3.257 (Mocha). CEILING: it must stay QUIETER on `--color-card` than the FOCUS RING, or a resting edge outshouts the one state that must read as focused — 6.22 vs 6.82 (Hearth), 5.67 vs 6.27 (Light), 6.14 vs 6.65 (Mocha). ONE DARK ARM SERVES BOTH DARK SEEDS (measured: Mocha clears on the Hearth arm, 3.257), so there is no mocha value-set row.

selection-quiet.$description: THE QUIET SELECTION FILL (#1110, owner ruling 2026-09-02) — the opaque, polarity-aware ground a BULK-DEFAULT selection control paints when it is ON. Backup & Restore's eleven-row "Include" fieldset is all-selected by default, so the accent skin spent the ember eleven times on the state the user has not chosen yet; `checkbox/variants.ts`'s `quiet` tone paints this instead. POLARITY-AWARE via CSS light-dark() (arg order light-arm FIRST, dark-arm second, the destructive convention above): a mark that INVERTS against its own fill cannot be one static grey — the dark arm oklch(0.66 0.005 70) is a light grey that reads ON against near-black chrome, the light arm oklch(0.54 0.008 70) a mid grey that reads ON against a near-white card. IT IS OPAQUE ON PURPOSE. The first cut was `bg-foreground/55`, an ALPHA tint whose real colour is whatever is behind it, so the pair could not be measured once — it had to be re-measured per ground (`alpha-token-needs-composited-contrast-probe`). An opaque token makes the pair a fact. BOUNDED FROM BOTH SIDES, which is what makes it a measurement and not a taste. CEILING: it must stay QUIETER than the accent checked fill on every seed, or the arm has no reason to exist — measured against `--color-card`: 5.759 vs the accent's 6.836 (Hearth), 4.994 vs 6.264 (Light), 5.687 vs 6.658 (Mocha). FLOOR: WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of the thing that identifies a control, and its worst ground is the `bg-accent` an interactive row paints on hover — 4.618 / 4.119 / 4.528.

selection-quiet-foreground.$description: The mark ON `--color-selection-quiet` — the check/dash glyph of a quiet bulk-default selection control. A PAIR ink: it only ever sits on its own fill, which is why it carries the `-foreground` suffix that `seed-theme-ink-contrast` reads as "judge this against its fill, not against neutral chrome" (lib/seed-theme-ink.ts inkTokensIn). The pair clears AA-NORMAL 4.5:1 in every shipped seed — 6.145 (Hearth), 4.781 (Light), 6.145 (Mocha) — so it is judged at the TEXT bar even though a checkmark would only owe 1.4.11's 3:1. Polarity-aware for the same reason its ground is: the light arm oklch(0.98 0.004 75) is near-white ink on the mid-grey light fill, the dark arm oklch(0.17 0.008 70) near-black on the light-grey dark fill.

sidebar.$description: deeper than content — the RAIL/LIST chrome

sidebar-accent-foreground.$description: Ink for controls painted on the sidebar accent surface

backdrop.$description: the polarity-FIXED dimming smoke — modal/drawer/select backdrops, the shell dismiss scrim, the wallpaper-dim layer, and both text-shadow halos (shell over-photo + wordmark; owner fence 2026-08-18: every already-correct scrim job keeps this exact value, byte-identical across the rename) (D43 §11.4 — never bg-black/50). Dimming means darker BY DESIGN, in every palette (the light seed deliberately keeps a dark smoke). It was `--color-scrim`, retired at #204: that one name also served as the transcript's over-art READING plate, whose polarity must FOLLOW the palette — one token cannot be a fixed dimmer and a polarity-following plate, and the overloaded name is how the bug was born (the photo-backing author reached for the token literally named scrim). A text PLATE over art rides color.reading-plate, never this.

reading-plate.$description: the transcript's over-art text backing (#204) — DERIVED, never designed: background + THEME_DERIVATION.readingPlate.deltaL (−0.038) at its solved alpha, so the plate always carries the palette's own polarity. This literal must equal that derivation off color.background; palette-contrast.suite.test.ts proves its paired reading-plate-foreground clears over black and white art, and ThemeScope emits the same pair for custom/carried themes. NOT color.backdrop (the fixed smoke): a token names ONE polarity semantic.

reading-plate-foreground.$description: the neutral ink paired with color.reading-plate and color.reading-band (#969). It is a distinct semantic because a translucent plate composited over art is not color.background: ThemeScope solves this ink against the plate over black and white art, while the three seeded palettes preserve their existing foreground pixels. Owner custom CSS may override it in the later winning plane.

reading-band.$description: The opaque sticky attribution backing: the reading plate's color at READING_BAND_ALPHA, derived from background with THEME_DERIVATION.readingPlate.deltaL. Opacity occludes scrolling prose; sharing the plate color prevents a second surface step. ThemeScope emits the same derivation for custom themes, paired with color.reading-plate-foreground.

sheen.$description: POLARITY-FIXED sheen highlight — the deliberate white gloss at the FOOT of a gradient-border glow (the CTA ring, the active tab, the active rail button), where the head is the theme's own --color-primary. Opaque here; each site applies its own alpha through the relative-color form `oklch(from var(--color-sheen) l c h / 0.0N)`, so the three tuned alphas (0.04/0.02/0.03) stay per-site while the HUE is one decision. It was three bare `oklch(1 0 0 / 0.0N)` literals sitting beside token-derived halves — invisible to every theme, including a light one where a white gloss is a no-op. A theme that wants a polarity-aware gloss overrides this var; the seed value-sets do NOT carry it (no per-theme variance today, and they are restricted to the ThemeScope-emitted class + color.backdrop).

shadow-hairline.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: the 1px edge-light ring of shadow.overlay. Polarity-FOLLOWING, and it is why this exists as a colour token at all (#232): Tailwind v4 INLINES a `--shadow-*` @theme value into the `.shadow-*` utility at build time, so a `[data-theme]` override of --shadow-overlay is a no-op for every consumer that uses the utility — a var() INGREDIENT survives the inlining and resolves at runtime. On a dark plate the ring is white-alpha edge light; on a light plate a white hairline is invisible (measured 1.29:1 against the page) and the ring must be a dark alpha instead, which is what the light value-set carries.

shadow-highlight.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: shadow.overlay's inset top-highlight (the light-from-above cue). Polarity-FOLLOWING for the same reason as shadow-hairline; a light palette spends its elevation budget on the ring instead, because a white top-highlight on a near-white card paints nothing.

shadow-ambient-near.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: shadow.overlay's tight CONTACT shadow (0 2px 4px). Carries its own alpha, because the alpha IS the per-polarity decision — a dark UI's float earns a heavy near-black contact layer, a light one reads as a torn-out sticker at the same value (home-delta 2026-08-18).

shadow-ambient-far.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: shadow.overlay's deep AMBIENT drop (0 12px 32px) — the loudest layer, and the one that threw a visible halo ~14px past the card box under the Light seed while it still wore this dark recipe. Alpha per polarity, same as shadow-ambient-near.

shadow-cta-highlight.$description: the ELEVATION INGREDIENT: the primary CTA's inset top-highlight (shadow.cta / shadow.cta-glow). Distinct from shadow-highlight because it catches on the PRIMARY fill, not on a surface — the light seed's darker primary takes a slightly stronger catch.

chart-1.$description: Chart ramp step 1 (ember) — polarity-aware categorical fill. The dark arm is the original value byte-identical; the darker light arm clears WCAG 1.4.11 against every legal light chart host while the five hues remain mutually distinguishable.

chart-2.$description: Chart ramp step 2 (muted teal) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

chart-3.$description: Chart ramp step 3 (dusty violet) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

chart-4.$description: Chart ramp step 4 (sage) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

chart-5.$description: Chart ramp step 5 (clay) — polarity-aware; dark arm byte-identical. See chart-1.

track-1.$description: D71 track ramp step 1 — a 6-step CATEGORICAL ramp for pool/meter/clock FILLS in the tracker block kit; also serves future charts. Pools are user-defined data and need a stable categorical color, assigned by definition order. NOW POLARITY-AWARE `light-dark(<light-arm>, <dark-arm>)` (the divergent-intent shape, not the plain chart-* value): the RULING SURVIVED, its INPUT changed (#697). The old ruling (a single mid-L value; 'a fill is never rendered as text so the value TEXT beside it carries meaning') is superseded — the gauge FILL is itself a non-text UI component under WCAG 1.4.11, and at mid-L these steps rendered 1.89–2.65:1 against the LIGHT panel (sidebar/surface-raised), below the 3:1 minimum, while measuring 5.9–9.3:1 on dark. The DARK arm is byte-identical to the original ramp (dark render unchanged); the LIGHT arm darkens each hue (keeping hue, keeping chroma where the sRGB gamut allows) to clear ≥3:1 against every light backing (panels + the bg-input rail composited over them, worse of float+8bit), while the 6 hues stay mutually distinguishable — the categorical mechanism is intact, only the light polarity is retuned. The active arm follows color-scheme (base :root dark, [data-theme=light] flips to light; the clamp derives it for custom themes, the intent-token precedent). Base-only (NOT in THEME_SCOPE_EMIT_VARS); any seed theme json MAY still override. Dark arm = the v2 mockup stand-in (--track-1, vitality green).

track-2.$description: D71 track ramp step 2 (resolve blue) — polarity-aware light arm to clear 1.4.11 on the light panel, dark arm byte-identical; see track-1.

track-3.$description: D71 track ramp step 3 (supply gold) — light arm at c 0.11 (one gamut step under the dark arm's 0.12 at this lower L); see track-1.

track-4.$description: D71 track ramp step 4 (corruption violet) — see track-1.

track-5.$description: D71 track ramp step 5 (rose) — see track-1.

track-6.$description: D71 track ramp step 6 (teal) — light arm at c 0.09 (one gamut step under the dark arm's 0.10 at this lower L); see track-1.

sky-day.$description: ATMOSPHERIC set (Waystone, side-eye ROOT CAUSE 2026-08-01): a small dedicated sky palette, because the stone was painting its sky with the CATEGORICAL chart ramp (track-*) mixed toward --color-background — which inverted day/night on the Light seed (midnight rendered LIGHTER than noon). POLARITY-FIXED by design and base-only (the track-*/chart-* precedent: NOT in THEME_SCOPE_EMIT_VARS, no seed override): night is dark in every theme, because a night sky IS dark — the stone's CHROME (ring, bezel, horizon, text) stays theme-reactive, its SKY does not. sky-day = the daylight zenith.

sky-day-horizon.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the pale band where a daylight sky meets the horizon (see sky-day).

sky-night.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — THE NIGHT ANCHOR (see sky-day). The one value the whole night half derives from; polarity-fixed dark so midnight can never render lighter than noon.

sky-night-horizon.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the lighter band above a night horizon (see sky-day).

sky-ember.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the golden-hour fire at dawn/dusk (see sky-day).

sky-ember-deep.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the deep red band under a golden hour (see sky-day).

sky-twilight.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — the violet wedge between dusk and full night (see sky-day).

sky-star.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — starlight: the NIGHT ANCHOR's contrast partner, never --color-foreground (which flips dark on a light theme and turned the stars into dirt). See sky-day.

sky-cloud.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — a lit cloud deck (see sky-day).

sky-cloud-dark.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — a storm deck: DARKER than the lit one (they were inverted, so storm clouds were the brightest thing in the sky). See sky-day.

sky-rain.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — falling water: a desaturated blue-grey, not the categorical teal it used to borrow. See sky-day.

sky-ash.$description: ATMOSPHERIC — ashfall motes: dark grit (they were bright peach confetti). See sky-day.

dialogue.$description: amber-gold quoted speech — the ONE saturated prose voice on the warm-neutral page (chroma 0.10 vs narration 0.02); ST quote-amber lineage. Owner-picked 2026-07-31. Was {color.foreground} (a visual no-op). D44 §12.1 dialogueColor (D44 §12.1 dialogueColor)

tone-solid.$description: D336 tone role: the tone's filled surface. A colored tone paints its intent base; neutral paints the page ink as a fill. Resolves on the nearest [data-tone] element.

tone-solid-hover.$description: D336 tone role: the solid under the pointer. A colored tone mixes away from the page ink; neutral mixes toward the page, by its own knob the ThemeScope clamp raises until its ink clears.

tone-solid-active.$description: D336 tone role: the pressed solid, one step past the hover.

tone-text.$description: D336 tone role: the tone's ink on the page family (background, raised, card), the popover and the sidebar.

tone-text-on-tint.$description: D336 tone role: the tone's ink on its own tints.

tone-tint.$description: D336 tone role: an opaque wash of the tone over its host, the surface under it (--tone-host, set by a tone-host-* utility, else the page), for a soft fill. It never carries meaning alone. A colored tone floors it under the page-family inks (pageInks) a selected row or an active tab keeps on it.

tone-tint-active.$description: D336 tone role: the tint one step stronger, for a hovered, pressed or selected soft fill. A colored tone floors it under the page-family inks (pageInks) a hovered or pressed row keeps on it.

tone-edge.$description: D336 tone role: the tone's held-back edge for an outline or a soft box, mixed over its host like the tints. It never carries meaning alone.

tone-foreground.$description: D336 tone role: the ink paired with the solid and its hover and active steps.

tone-mix.$description: D336 tone-role mix amounts: the share of the tone's base (or, for neutral's solid steps, of the page ink) in each role's color-mix(). The ThemeScope clamp re-solves the text, tint and neutral knobs for a carried background and emits them on the scope.

hover.$description: a colored solid under the pointer: the base's share, the rest the endpoint away from the page ink.

neutral-hover.$description: the neutral solid under the pointer: the page ink's share, the rest the page. The clamp raises it until the page-colored ink clears.

text.$description: a tone's ink on the page family: the base's share, the rest the page ink.

text-on-tint.$description: a tone's ink on its own tint: less base than the page ink, because the tint spends some of the pair's contrast.

tint.$description: a soft fill: the base's share over the page.

tint-active.$description: a hovered, pressed or selected soft fill.

edge.$description: a held-back tone edge over the page.

primitive.$description: The ramps (docs/law/UI-Density-Law.md §2.4). Only a primitive holds a raw dimension; every semantic spacing, size, radius, text and leading token aliases one step. space, size and leading steps are named by their CSS px at the 16px root; radius and type are ordinal.

tight.$description: intent token — ATOM gaps inside an island (label↔bar, glyph↔text, value↔caption). UI-Density-Law.md §2.2/D2: the mocks' instrument internals cluster at 3–5px (`.meter` gap 3px, `.rel` gap 4px, `.chip` gap 4px), below `field`, so they either rounded up (visibly loose) or went raw (gate-red). 4px is the 4pt sub-grid floor. `field` (6px) deliberately STAYS 6px — with `tight` added it is the 2pt sub-step (Carbon spacing-01 precedent, D3).

field.$description: intent token — within a labeled field

row.$description: intent token — items in a row

block.$description: intent token — blocks in a stack

section.$description: intent token — sections in a surface

density-section-compact.$description: the compact arm of the section spacing intent. The other compact density arms reuse existing canonical spacing steps; this is the one value the scale did not already contain. Consumed only through the generated private density aliases in orb.cssValues.

$extensions.orb.purpose: a pointer-conditional or density-conditional arm

glyph-gap.$description: the gap between two adjacent glyph buttons that keeps their touch-floor hit areas apart — POINTER-CONDITIONAL, the touch-target minus glyph-lg: 12px at coarse/unknown pointers, 6px at fine via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override. touch-target.$description: the ≥44px touch floor — POINTER-CONDITIONAL (D62 P1, §4b axis 3): the 44px value holds by default (coarse/unknown pointers); fine pointers narrow it to 28px via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override. tests/client/features/app-shell/touch-target-floor.suite.ct.tsx asserts the floor at a coarse pointer.

control-sm.$description: control-height — POINTER-CONDITIONAL (D62 P1): 44px at coarse (meets the touch floor), 32px at fine via the @media(pointer:fine) override. The fine value is the design-audit tap-target hard floor (TAP_FAIL_PX=32, WCAG 2.5.8's 24px + repo margin) — it was 28px (Task #76: two side-eye passes + design-audit flagged every compact/icon control below the floor). compact density tightens via data-density, orthogonal to pointer.

control-md.$description: control-height — POINTER-CONDITIONAL (D62 P1): 48px at coarse, 36px at fine via the @media(pointer:fine) override. The fine ramp is 32/36/40, a 4px ladder; the `icon` button size rides this step.

avatar-sm.$description: avatar DISPLAY size — decoupled from control heights (§13.9 D62 delta): pointer-independent, never narrows. 24px — character-bar overlap chips

avatar-hero.$description: 64px — the character-detail hero avatar. The display-only hero size L1 deferred to the surface lane that needed it; still pointer-independent (a display glyph, not a touch target), same as the sm/md/lg trio.

switch-track.$description: the Switch VISIBLE track WIDTH — POINTER-CONDITIONAL since #420: 64px at coarse, 48px at fine via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override. It was pointer-INDEPENDENT at 48px until 2026-08-22, and that is precisely what broke: once the ROOT began carrying the ≥44px coarse floor on its HEIGHT (`pointer-coarse:h-touch-target`, 96d167e407) a 48-wide track around a 32px thumb became a 1.091-aspect near-circle with track painting on all four sides of the knob — side-eye #420 measured it and called it a crescent moon, not a switch, on every touch surface. The WIDTH now scales with the height so the control keeps a switch's silhouette (64x44, aspect 1.455) and the travel stays legible (travel = switch-track − switch-track-height — 20px at coarse and 16px at fine — since #1109 gave the knob its own equal inset on all four sides, which absorbs both the border and the pointer arm; it was switch-track − switch-thumb while the thumb was flush with the track's height). The FINE arm is byte-identical to what it always was (48x32, travel 16) — #371's fine-pointer receipts hold unchanged.

switch-track-height.$description: the Switch VISIBLE track HEIGHT — POINTER-CONDITIONAL: 44px at coarse, 32px at fine via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override. MINTED at #1109 (owner ruling 2026-09-02) by splitting the job out of --size-switch-thumb, which was ONE token doing TWO — the fine-pointer track height AND the thumb size at every pointer — so the knob structurally could not scale with the pointer. Its coarse arm and --size-touch-target's coarse arm alias the same primitive step, and the root's height is now spelled from this token alone (it used to be `h-switch-thumb pointer-coarse:h-touch-target`, two utilities for one dimension, with an unknown-pointer arm that got the coarse WIDTH and the fine HEIGHT). Height and WIDTH (--size-switch-track) are the pair that owns the silhouette: 64x44 coarse (aspect 1.455), 48x32 fine (1.5), both past the >1.4 floor side-eye #420 minted against the crescent moon. The thumb's travel is exactly switch-track − switch-track-height (20px coarse, 16px fine) because the knob is inset equally on all four sides — the derivation is in packages/ui/src/primitives/switch/variants.ts and holds at both pointers. A conformant DTCG dimension in the token vault, the one home for a reusable portable value (client-architecture-lockdown.md §4).

switch-inset.$description: 9px coarse / 6px fine — the gap the Switch's knob leaves on ALL FOUR sides of the track. The root spends it as inline padding (`px-switch-inset`) and the knob's own SIZE is derived from it at the site, so the block gap is this same quantity by construction. IT IS THE PRIMARY OF THE PAIR SINCE #1684 (owner ruling 2026-09-06): the knob used to be its own belted token (--size-switch-thumb, retired there) and the block gap fell out of `items-center` halving (switch-track-height - 2x border-width-control - switch-thumb) — three independently belted integers whose difference is EVEN only by luck, so at the font scales where it is odd the resting knob sat on a HALF pixel (fontScale 1.25, the `reading` appearance preset: content box 38, thumb 23, offset 1 + 7.5 = 8.5) and design-audit's `off-grid-transform` filed #1684 against the resting thumb on settings:appearance. The knob is now spelled `switch-track-height - 2x border-width-control - 2x this` in packages/ui/src/primitives/switch/variants.ts, so the centred difference is 2x this by construction and the rest landing is exactly border + inset — a whole pixel at EVERY font scale, which is the half of docs/law/integer-line-boxes.md §2's declared residual this control no longer carries. IT ALSO CARRIES THE #1109 OWNER RULING (2026-09-02) THE RETIRED TOKEN STATED: the knob is ~55% of --size-switch-track-height (18 in 32 fine = 56.25%, 24 in 44 coarse = 54.5% at the 16px root — byte-identical to what #1109 shipped), a knob in a track rather than a slab in a slot, which is also what gives a fill probe TRACK in the band around the knob instead of 72% PAGE (#1170). THE RELATIONS TO KEEP: the RENDERED left/right gap EQUALS the rendered top gap at both pointer classes, both land on whole device pixels at rest in both states, and the knob keeps its 0.45-0.65 share of the track. The knob's travel is switch-track - switch-track-height, which this quantity cancels out of (variants.ts derives it). An arbitrary `px-[calc(...)]` was the first spelling of the inline half and `no-raw-spacing-in-features` correctly refused it. A conformant DTCG dimension in the token vault (client-architecture-lockdown.md section 4).

media-spotlight.$description: 96px — the radius of the hover spotlight that follows the pointer over a media grid cell.

checkbox.$description: 18px — the Checkbox/Radio VISIBLE box (display size, §13.9 family: pointer-INDEPENDENT like avatars — NOT like the Switch, whose track and thumb both became pointer-conditional at #420/#1109). Decoupled from --spacing-section (it previously rode size-section, coupling the box to the GROUP-GAP intent token — retuning section spacing resized every checkbox). The ≥44px coarse hit floor is carried by the ::before size-touch-target pseudo, never this box. PP5 (D66).

slider-thumb.$description: 24px — the Slider VISIBLE thumb (display size, §13.9 family: pointer-INDEPENDENT like avatars/checkbox — switch-thumb left this list at #1109). Decoupled from --spacing-section (it previously rode size-section, the same GROUP-GAP coupling PP5 fixed for checkbox/radio — retuning section spacing resized every slider thumb; W2 flagged it). The ≥44px drag/hit floor is carried separately by the h-control-sm control row, never this thumb. Its HALF is --size-slider-inset; the two move together.

slider-inset.$description: 12px — HALF of --size-slider-thumb, and the margin the Slider's Control carries on both inline sides. Base UI centres each thumb ON its value position (left: pct% of the Control's padding box, shifted -50%), so at min and max the thumb hangs half its width OUTSIDE the Control. Measured at a 430px coarse viewport (side-eye 2026-08-22 P2-8): a full-bleed row put the max thumb at x 406→430 and the min thumb at 0→24 — flush with the screen edge, with its grabbable half sitting on the OS edge-swipe bezel. Insetting the Control by half a thumb pulls both extremes back inside the row; the rail shortens by one thumb width and nothing else moves. A step of its own rather than a calc: if slider-thumb changes, change this with it.

glyph-xs.$description: 16px — the SQUARE GLYPH-BUTTON box ramp (display size, §13.9 family: pointer-INDEPENDENT like avatars/checkbox/slider-thumb — switch-thumb left this list at #1109). A glyph button is an icon-only micro-affordance that rides INSIDE a dense row (a badge's dismiss, a tracker row's delete) and must not claim a control height: at `control-sm` the delete on a 20px badge would be taller than the badge. Deliberately NOT the avatar ramp — an avatar is a portrait size, and coupling the two means retuning character-bar chips resizes every delete button (the PP5 / slider-thumb lesson). The ≥ touch-floor hit area is carried by Button's `glyph-*` ::before touch-target pseudo, never this box. xs = the tightest step: a dismiss inside a `sm` Badge.

glyph-sm.$description: 20px — the glyph-button ramp's ROW step (pairs the family header): the trailing delete on a list row (quest, beat, pack item) and the RpgFieldLock pin. Holds a 12px `xs` Icon with a 4px optical surround.

glyph-md.$description: 24px — the glyph-button ramp's EDITOR step: an inline toolbar of icon toggles in a definition/editor row (band-visibility, story-lock, delete). Holds a 12px `xs` Icon with a 6px surround, and reads as a control without stealing the row's height.

glyph-lg.$description: 32px — the glyph-button ramp's PICKER step: a grid/strip of icon CHOICES where the glyph is the content being chosen (the pack icon picker), so it holds a 16px `sm` Icon and is the only step that also clears the fine-pointer tap floor on its own box.

These are NOT themeable (a theme is a value-set, never a structural mode — §4.1/§12.1); the css-structure test asserts shell.css consumes ONLY var(--dimension-*) for geometry. Not a Tailwind utility namespace — consumed via raw var(--dimension-*) in the one shell-tier CSS file.

rail.$description: the persistent thin icon-rail width (~56px, §4.1). Also the mobile bottom-tab-bar height.

chrome-row.$description: topbar + panel-header height — the chrome row (~48px). Was a bare 3rem literal duplicated 4× in shell.css.

panel-floor.$description: the RESPONSIVE FLOOR both side-panel clamps share — the narrowest a docked panel may ever be, and (since #242) the floor the conditional both-docked squeeze may not push the LIST panel past. Its own token because three sites must agree on one number: the two clamps below reference it, and shell.css's squeeze needs it as a bare value (a max() operand cannot read the floor back out of a clamp()).

device-pixel.$description: ONE DEVICE PIXEL AT DPR 1 — the grid a promoted layer's box must land on (docs/law/integer-line-boxes.md Laws 2 and 3). Its only job is to be the STEP argument of a round(): a viewport-derived clamp resolves fractional widths (24vw of 1280 is 307.1875), which lands the shell's panel tracks and their resting translations off the grid and disables text snapping (#1120). A whole CSS pixel is a whole device pixel at DPR 1 and an even one at DPR 2, so one step serves both. NOT a border width and never a spacing step: it is a quantum, not a distance. It is a TOKEN rather than a shell.css literal because a portable value belongs to the vault (client-architecture-lockdown.md §4), which is also what the css-length-tokens gate prescribes for it.

panel-context-step.$description: the CONTEXT pane's SQUEEZE FLOOR (#242) — and it is an owner ruling, not a taste pick: 3c49a6cce2 widened panel-context to 30vw precisely so a STANDARD 1280px desktop reaches 384px — the 24rem container step where the Waystone paints at its focal 120px. The #242 both-docked squeeze therefore takes its slack from the LIST pane first and stops at this step on the context side, rather than trading the rpg takeover's focal stone for reading width. Where the deficit outlives both floors the content track stays short — a shell-grid limit, stated, not faked.

content-reading-floor.$description: 648px — the CONTENT track width at which the transcript's REAL-CHARACTER reading floor is met (#242, owner-ruled off #240). Measured, not designed: at viewport 1360 / both panels docked the content track is 569.6px and the room's own prose renders 55.3 real characters per line; the recovery needed to reach 65 is +70px, measured in the CT against the transcript's actual glyphs (chat-room-track.suite.ct.tsx — the ruling's sketched +60 lands at 63.7 chars, 9.6px short, so the target is honoured rather than the estimate). The owner ruled this REAL-CHARACTER floor over the token-strict 65ch one (which needs ~+96px and would cost far more panel). Consumed ONLY by shell.css's conditional squeeze as the threshold — above it nothing moves, so a viewport where the floor already fits is byte-identical. In rem so it tracks appearance.fontScale, exactly like the ch-based measure it stands in for. RE-DERIVED POST-GEIST AND UNCHANGED (#1204, 2026-09-02): the ruling survives, its INPUT moved. Geist has a WIDE zero and NARROWER lowercase, so it split the two floors in opposite directions — 65 CSS ch went 557.7 -> 650px while 65 characters of the room's own prose went the other way and now measures 462px (chat-room-track's own LONG_PROSE sample in the bubble's 15px prose font, probe 2026-09-02). Track -> line on this grid is -60.6 (track to pane) -96 (a 48px avatar gutter, the 40px `lg` chip plus its 8px gap, + the flat skin's 2x px-section inset). The ruled 40rem was measured against the 32px chip; when the chip grew to 40px (the owner's Glimmer-preset ruling) the line lost those 8px and fell 2px under the floor at both-panels-open, so the threshold carries the same 8px: 40.5rem. The 65 ch floor stays the STATED RESIDUAL here and is answered where it belongs — dimension.shell-content-floor, the reader's own dial, below.

shell-content-floor.$description: 746px — the FLOOR of the reader's chat-width dial (`--width-shell-content`, app-shell.tsx's `clamp(<this>, <chatWidthPct>dvw, 100dvw)`), and the number is DERIVED, not picked (#1204, 2026-09-02). WHAT IT GUARANTEES: at the narrowest the dial goes, the transcript's line still holds reading.measure-min — the FLOOR of the transcript's own 65-75ch band — so the dial ranges the line across exactly that band instead of below it. THE ARITHMETIC, ALL OF IT MEASURED IN THE BUBBLE'S OWN PROSE FONT (Geist, --text-body 0.9375rem = 15px, where 1 CSS ch resolves to exactly 10px): 65ch = 650px, the row spends a 48px identity gutter (the 40px `lg` avatar chip, the default size since the owner's Glimmer-preset ruling, + its 8px gap, a SIBLING of the content column by law) and the flat skin's inner spends 2 x --spacing-section = 48px, so the track must be 650 + 48 + 48 = 746px. THE ECHO SKIN LANDS ON THE SAME NUMBER, which is the check that it is the right one: echo's box is `measure-min + art-width + block` = 854px and its art pane is additive, so at a 746px track its column (746 + 192 - 48 = 890px) finally clears that box and the prose reads 650px too — both skins at the floor exactly, neither below. WHY IT MOVED: the pre-Geist literal was 680px, which held 592px of flat prose and 628px of echo (probe 2026-09-02) — under 65ch for EVERY skin once `77e07912eb` shipped Geist and 65ch stepped 557.7 -> 650px. In rem, not px, so it tracks appearance.fontScale exactly like the ch-denominated measure it is derived from. It is a token rather than the app-shell literal it replaces because a portable value belongs to the vault (client-architecture-lockdown.md §4); the dial's OTHER two terms stay in the inline style because the middle one is the user's own percentage. It is NOT dimension.content-reading-floor: that one is the shell grid's squeeze threshold against the REAL-CHARACTER floor (#242's owner ruling) and is a different question with a different answer. #1728 ARM B RESTATES WHAT THIS FLOOR PROTECTS, AND THE ARITHMETIC ABOVE IS UNCHANGED (2026-09-05, owner ruling). The centred skins (flat/hush/document) stopped putting the identity chip inside the centred unit: at and above the `@4xl` container step (56rem = 896px) the row body is a three-rail grid whose MIDDLE rail is the reading column, so the column centres on its own and the chip hangs in the rail beside it -- measured, the flat column went 285/245 to 265/265 at a 1280px row and 157/117 to 137/137 at 1024, i.e. it no longer moves when `showInChatAvatars` is toggled. THAT DOES NOT TOUCH THIS NUMBER, and the reason is the crossover: 746px is BELOW 896px, so at the floor the chip is still IN FLOW and the row still spends `650 + 48 + 48 = 746` exactly as derived above. What changes is only what the track spends ABOVE the crossover, where the box is the 75ch cap plus the flat inset and the chip lives in the remainder rather than in the column's own line. The two regimes meet without a gap because the crossover was derived from the same measure: a 40px `size.avatar-lg` chip fits a margin once `(track - 75ch) / 2 >= 40`, i.e. at 830px, and the named step above that is 896px -- so the 830-896px band keeps the in-flow gutter, conservative by one step and never clipping. The bubble family is untouched and still spends the gutter in flow at every width, which is why this floor stays the floor for every skin.

$extensions.orb.purpose: a glass recipe ingredient

blur.$description: D44 §12.1 appearance.blurSurfaces: the glass recipe. Its ingredients are the saturate and the translucent fills here, the blur radius from the reader's `appearance.blurStrength` (`--appearance-blur-strength`), the existing --color-border hairline as the edge, and the blur-surface variants in client globals.css. Not a plain blur.

veil.$description: The boot veil's soft focus before it sharpens on entry (web-weave variants).

fill-chrome.$description: the translucent surface-fill mix percentage for PURE CHROME surfaces (panels/composer/modals) — `color-mix(in oklab, var(--color-surface) 70%, transparent)`. The Reading-Surface rule (after Marinara): chrome gets a LIGHTER fill than text-heavy surfaces.

fill-dense.$description: the translucent surface-fill mix percentage for TEXT-HEAVY surfaces (messages, when opted in) — more opaque than fill-chrome so scrolling prose stays legible over the blur (after Marinara's variable glass opacity).

fill-contrast.$description: the fill-chrome and fill-dense mix percentage while increased contrast resolves on (client globals.css, the appearance-increased-contrast variant) — denser glass so edges and ink read against the art behind it.

fill-solid.$description: the fill-chrome and fill-dense mix percentage while reduced transparency resolves on (client globals.css, the appearance-reduced-transparency variant) — fully opaque, so every surface stays tinted as itself.

saturate.$description: the glass recipe's backdrop saturation boost — the 4th ingredient beside strength/fill-chrome/fill-dense; consumed as saturate(var(--blur-saturate)) at every backdrop-filter site.

immersive.$description: Phase 4 §B.2 chatStyle immersive-mode geometry, REDONE for readability (the reading-surface rule — art fades to a clean surface BEFORE the text, never under it) — the per-mode avatar/decoration dimensions for Echo/Whisper/Hush/Ripple, tokenized so no magic px/%/hex lands in message-row-variants.ts (§B.6 'no hardcoded magic numbers'). Tide's per-paragraph train gap reuses the existing spacing.field intent token — no new geometry needed there.

echo-art-width.$description: Echo: the ART PANE's own width — a FIXED column beside the prose, never a percentage of the bubble (#212). It was `echo-feather: 55%`, spent as the bubble's `padding-right` inside a `max-w-prose` box: 55% of 558px is 307px of padding, so the reading line rendered 239px = 28 characters against the house 65-75ch law, and the same percentage made the art box grow with the message (a 400x600 portrait painted into a 558x2965 `cover` box = a 4.94x upscale cropped past the subject's head). Now the art sits OUTSIDE the measure: the bubble's max-width is `65ch + this` (the prose measure is untouched), the padding on the art side is exactly this width, the feather gradient's stop is this width, and the art layer is painted at `this auto` anchored to its top outer corner — so the portrait is DOWN-scaled from its 400px request and the subject stays in frame at any message length. Consumed by message-row-variants.ts as the pane's padding and reach, and by the art tile in message-row-bubble.tsx.

echo-art-height-phone.$description: 250px — Echo's art pane height on a phone, Moonlit Echoes' mobile default (`--custom-EchoAvatarMobileHeight`): the pane keeps its width and the art fills this height, cover-cropped, instead of a short corner thumbnail.

whisper-banner-viewport-cap.$description: Whisper identity art takes at most one eighth of the small viewport height, leaving the short-height transcript room for its identity header and prose.

whisper-feather.$description: Whisper: the gradient stop (of `whisper-banner-height`, the band's own box) where the art fully dissolves into the bubble's own bg color, softening the band→text transition.

stripe-width.$description: 3px — the speaker-colour (--color-speaker) tick's thickness, measured on the Moonlit Echoes Hush and Whisper captures (3px wide).

whisper-band-opacity.$description: Whisper's banner image at rest, from the Moonlit parity item 0880 (0.8 opacity; the captures do not show it). Hover returns it to full.

whisper-band-min-height-phone.$description: 125px — Whisper's banner minimum height on a phone, from the Moonlit parity item 0880 (the banner grows to 55% of the card, at least this tall; the captures do not show it).

$extensions.orb.purpose: a reading measure or bubble share

reading.$description: The reading measures the transcript and prose columns cap at. The reader's own line-height, letter-spacing and paragraph-spacing are appearance settings (`--appearance-reading-*`, the client appearance channel), not tokens. THE READING-SURFACE RULE: this group governs spacing/sizing only — blur/glow never land on the reading surface.

measure-ch.$description: Portable character-count decision for the CHAT TRANSCRIPT reading measure. It was the app's ONE line-length cap until #1145 (owner ruling 2026-09-02): CSS `ch` is the zero-glyph advance, so 75ch reads 107-117 TYPOGRAPHIC characters and no paragraph capped here can meet the design law's 65-75 band. The measure was SPLIT rather than narrowed — transcripts keep 75ch because dialogue reads differently (short attributed lines, not continuous body copy) — and teaching/body prose moved to reading.measure-prose-ch (47ch), which carries the arithmetic. Emitted as --reading-measure and consumed by the transcript's content column (client globals.css). A measure belongs on the PARAGRAPH, never on the page — a ch resolves in the element's own font, so the cap must sit on the prose element itself or it reads at the wrong scale.

measure-prose-ch.$description: Portable character-count decision for the TEACHING/BODY-PROSE reading measure — the second of the app's two measures (#1145, owner ruling 2026-09-02: SPLIT the token, do not narrow the transcript). Emitted as --reading-measure-prose. THE ARITHMETIC, ALL OF IT MEASURED: CSS `ch` is the advance of the zero glyph, which in Geist is 0.6625em (canvas, live client, 100px and 400px). The design law's 65-75 characters per line is the AVERAGE GLYPH ADVANCE, which across the app's own prose runs 0.4248em (the densest real copy — home's temp-chat gloss, measured in home-surface.ct.tsx) to 0.4629em (a pangram). One CSS ch is therefore 1.43-1.56 law-characters, and reading.measure-ch's 75ch reads 107-117 of them: the CT measures exactly 117.0 at 1920, so no paragraph capped at 75ch can meet the law at any font size. 47ch = 31.14em = 67.3 law-characters at the loosest sample and 73.3 at the densest — inside the 65-75 band at BOTH ends, with margin. 48ch was the ruling's estimate; it lands the densest copy at 74.9, i.e. on the ceiling with a tenth of a character to spare, so the derived value is 47. Transcripts keep reading.measure-ch (dialogue is short attributed lines, not continuous body copy); teaching copy, glosses, empty-state explanations and every other non-transcript reading paragraph take this one. See client-architecture-lockdown.md §4 for which CSS home may spell it.

$extensions.orb.purpose: one meaning of an element's opacity (receded, faint, disabled, dragging, loading, hover, grain)

opacity.$description: Element opacity by meaning, never by number. A feature never picks an opacity step; it passes the primitive's `receded` prop. A recipe or stylesheet in @orb/ui spells the step that names what its element is (`opacity-disabled`, `data-loading:opacity-loading`), and an element whose meaning is none of these keeps `opacity-0` or `opacity-100`. A keyframe waypoint is an animation value, not a meaning, and stays a literal.

receded.$description: a receded element: an archived row, a secondary glyph. It stands behind its siblings and keeps its place in the reading order.

faint.$description: chrome that only hints at itself: a secondary mark on touch, where there is no hover to reveal it, a glow layer resting behind its island, and the fill of a set neutral slider, whose weight beside its full-ink thumb says the knob is set. Fainter than receded, which still reads as content.

disabled.$description: a control, label or item that cannot be used right now. A row of content that stands behind its siblings is receded instead.

dragging.$description: an item held by a drag, so the gap it left and the place it will land stay readable. Not disabled: the item is in use.

loading.$description: a surface waiting on work it started, dimmed a step so the wait reads as in progress without hiding what is there.

hover.$description: the dim a quiet part gives under the pointer: art that is its own tap target answers a hover by easing back a step instead of gaining a tint.

quiet.$description: text one step quieter than its siblings that must still read as body text: a caption in a rail that does not hold the current view, while it rests: hover, focus and the active state stand it down. Any lower step puts a muted ink under the 4.5:1 text floor.

resting.$description: the mark of a control that is off: a switch thumb. It carries no information, so it stays under the on state's loudest member while holding 3:1 against its track.

held.$description: a mark that animates in and out, held in its drawn pose when motion is reduced, so the state it signals stays visible without moving.

grain.$description: the strength of the surface grain film laid over the shell and cards, a texture that must never read as a pattern.

control.$description: the STRUCTURAL border a control root paints (the Switch track today). A border-box root's border is ARITHMETIC, not just paint: the Switch's content box is 2× this narrower than --size-switch-track, and the thumb's travel calc must subtract it or the checked knob lands one border-width proud of the right rim. The root spells its width from this same token, so the geometry and the paint can never drift apart. It aliases `default`: a plain `border` on a neighbouring field and a control root's own border are one weight, and the sizes derived from it follow a retuned default. The alias resolves when the tokens build, so a stylesheet that overrides only `--border-width-default` at runtime leaves this one behind. Consumed via var(--border-width-control), never a raw 1px.

The ring's weight is `border-width.rule`, written `ring-(length:--border-width-rule)` and `outline-(length:--border-width-rule)`; this group holds what the weight does not: how far the ring stands from the box it marks. field.$description: the type step a native form control paints at — POINTER-CONDITIONAL (§4b axis 3, the size.touch-target precedent). 16px at coarse because iOS Safari ZOOMS THE VIEWPORT IN when a control under 16px takes focus and never zooms back out (#1868: the owner reported it as three symptoms — pinch-to-recover, a tab bar below the fold, and sideways panning — which are one cause, since a zoomed page pans and the app has no horizontal scroll container at all); 15px at fine via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override, which is where the design's own body step lives. It is a SEPARATE token from text.body and not a pointer arm ON text.body, because message-bubble reads text.body for transcript prose — a coarse arm there would enlarge all reading prose on touch and collide with the reader's own --appearance-reading-body-scale dial. ROOT-FLOORED SINCE #1872: the coarse arm is emitted max(1rem, 16px), because :root font-size is calc(100% * var(--appearance-font-scale)) and appearance.fontScale bottoms out at 0.8 — so the lower 40% of that slider (0.95 -> 15.2px, 0.80 -> 12.8px) silently re-armed the very zoom this token exists to prevent. The floor is derived from this token's own authored value and the PAIRED leading.field is floored identically, so the face:leading ratio is the authored 24/16 = 1.5 at EVERY stop of the slider rather than the 1.0 a face-only max() would have produced at 0.8. The fine arm is deliberately NOT floored — a mouse has no focus-zoom.

field-dense.$description: the DENSE field step — the instrument tier's pane chrome and the input `inline` click-to-edit arm. POINTER-CONDITIONAL for the same reason as text.field and to the same 16px coarse floor; 13px at fine, which is the step that keeps a LIST pane's search box from outshouting the 13px row titles it filters (side-eye P1-1). The two arms are what let that intent survive on a mouse and yield on a finger: at coarse it converges with text.field, because a platform floor is not negotiable by density. ROOT-FLOORED SINCE #1872 for the same reason and by the same derivation as text.field — a platform floor is not negotiable by appearance.fontScale either; paired with leading.field-dense, so the floored region holds the authored 20/16 = 1.25 ratio.

code-field.$description: the type step a MONOSPACE text-ENTRY surface paints at — text.field's code-voice twin, POINTER-CONDITIONAL for exactly the same platform reason (#2450). text.code stays 13px at every pointer because it is a READING voice (inline code in prose, a log line, a tool-call block) and a coarse arm there would enlarge all of that on touch — the same objection text.field records against putting a coarse arm on text.body. But two surfaces paint mono type a finger FOCUSES — the CodeEditor's contenteditable and the NumberField `inline` arm — and iOS Safari zooms the viewport in on any focused editable under 16px and never zooms back out. So the ENTRY voice gets its own token: 16px at coarse, 13px at fine via the emitted @media(pointer:fine) override, which is byte-identical to what those surfaces painted before, so nothing moves on a mouse. ROOT-FLOORED for text.field's reason (#1872): :root font-size is calc(100% * var(--appearance-font-scale)) and appearance.fontScale bottoms out at 0.8, which would silently re-arm the very zoom this token prevents; the PAIRED leading.code-field is floored identically so the face:leading ratio is the authored 24/16 = 1.5 at every stop of the slider. The fine arm is deliberately NOT floored — a mouse has no focus-zoom.

field.$description: text.field's paired leading — 24px on the 16px coarse step (1.50), 23px on the 15px fine step (1.53). Snapped, like every other leading (docs/law/integer-line-boxes.md Law 1). ROOT-FLOORED SINCE #1872 AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE FLOOR: text.field alone floored at 16px inside a 0.8-scaled 20px line box would be ratio 1.0 — cramped, and the shape #1872 refuses. Flooring the PAIR from each token's own authored value keeps the coarse arm at exactly 24/16 = 1.50 everywhere below --appearance-font-scale 1, identical to what it resolves to at 1. Belt order is round(up, max(1.5rem, 24px), 1px): the floor picks the length, the belt puts it on the device-pixel grid.

field-dense.$description: text.field-dense's paired leading. The fine arm is 16px on the 13px step (1.23), the dense control rhythm. The COARSE arm is 20px on the 16px platform floor (1.25) — the same dense rhythm, NOT the prose one. It shipped at 24px (1.50) for one afternoon and that was a reasoned guess, not a measurement, and it was wrong in a way that only showed up on the DENSITY axis: 24px is +8px over the fine arm, while compact density's whole --spacing-field is 4px, so a single leading jump was twice the entire padding saving compact exists to make. The owner reported it as 'in compact it is somehow more comfortable', which is exactly what a control that grows 8px taller regardless of density feels like. 1.25rem is a step the scale already carries (leading.label-relaxed's value), so no new number is minted to fix it. ROOT-FLOORED SINCE #1872, paired with text.field-dense, so the coarse arm holds 20/16 = 1.25 at every --appearance-font-scale below 1 instead of collapsing toward 1.0.

control-col.$description: 200px — the COLUMN WIDTH of a horizontal settings row: its control column in every mode, and (since #932) the LABEL track too, because a settings row's name and its control are the same order of width and one token spent twice is what gives a whole pane ONE control edge (measured: Appearance 799px x16 and Chat behavior 799px x15, against the five and four edges the #1099 re-drive censused). It governs the control column in BOTH of the row's alignment modes, and the modes read it differently on purpose (#932): FieldLayout align=block (the pre-#932 default, UIP-404) consumes it as a FIXED width via w-(--width-control-col), docking the control at the row's right edge; FieldLayout align=track consumes it as the fit-content LIMIT of the section's shared control track (gridVariants cols=settingTrack), so the widest control in the section sizes the track and every row starts its control at the same x while nothing is stretched past this cap. One decision, one token, two readings — a section that mixes the modes still agrees about how wide a control column may get. Consumed by @orb/ui Field (orientation=horizontal) + SettingRow/SettingRowGroup; never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

label-col.$description: 152px — the LEFT label column of an instrument knob row (the preset params deck's KnobRow): the mirror of width.control-col, sized so a column of knob labels reads down one edge while the slider keeps the middle. DISTINCT from control-col (that is the settings row's control column, and a knob row's control is the flexing track, not a fixed column). NOT the settings row's label track: #932 measured a 152px limit wrapping five of fifteen Chat-behavior labels to two lines ('Send continues the reply', 'Empty Enter generates a reply', 'Auto-swipe short replies', 'Custom stopping strings', 'Offer choices in new chats'), so that track takes width.control-col instead — a knob CAPTION and a settings row's NAME are different lengths, and this token stays the knob one. Consumed via w-(--width-label-col); never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

content-col.$description: 720px — the MEASURE cap for an editor's CONTENT column (the preset editor's five views; the width every preset-redesign mock draws its content panel at). A pane wider than this stretched knob rows to ~840px with a ~60% dead gutter and ran explanatory glosses to ~130ch against the 65-75ch reading measure (side-eye F-16, 2026-08-02). The column is CENTERED (mx-auto — the character editor's own convention) and breathes to width.content-col-wide once its container clears @5xl. ONE RATIFIED EXCEPTION to the breathe (#1682): an INSTRUMENT whose only flexing cell is a control track holds this cap and does NOT breathe — it stays centered inside the breathing column, because every surplus pixel would go into the track and a dial gets harder to aim as it grows. The ratified site is the Params deck (packages/client/src/features/preset/components/params-deck.tsx, side-eye 2026-08-19 P2), which argues it at its own site and fences it with a CT; a consumer count that reads that site as a missing breathe is reading this exception. Consumed via max-w-(--width-content-col); never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

content-col-wide.$description: 896px — the BREATHE step of width.content-col, applied only once the content pane itself clears the @5xl container breakpoint (i.e. panels collapsed). A fixed 720 clamp inside a ~1520px pane left ~800px of dead void (owner, 2026-08-02: 'looks okay when both panels are out, but when you close them it looks awful'). 56rem keeps explanatory glosses inside the ~65-75ch reading measure at the deck's 13px step while the knob rows stop looking marooned. Consumed via @5xl:max-w-(--width-content-col-wide); never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

Sized to hold the widest datum the deck feeds it (a grouped 6-digit context window, "131,072") at the `code` type step plus its padding, so a column of knob rows aligns on one number edge. Consumed by @orb/ui NumberField's size axis; never a raw bracket (gate no-arbitrary-tw-values).

--aspect-banner.description: the 3:1 Whisper header-BAND aspect — pairs with the server's smart-cropped 3:1 `blobBannerUrl` variant so the displayed band matches the source crop at ANY bubble width (height DERIVES from width, exactly like `aspect-portrait`). Replaces a fixed band height, which drifted the box aspect off 3:1 as the fluid-width bubble changed and made `background-size:cover` re-crop the already-tight face-safe source. Still a REAL block-level child with a definite box (aspect-ratio gives it height), so text stays in normal flow BELOW it — the Phase-4 anti-squish property is preserved. Emits `--aspect-banner` (the `--aspect-*` theme namespace).

--dimension-panel.purpose: a shell geometry input (rail, chrome row, panel clamp, reading floor, device pixel)
--dimension-panel.description: the LIST side-panel track width (§11.1 clamp-overlay). The CONTEXT panel has its own, wider clamp — see panel-context. This is the IDEAL; at both-docked it is also the pane that gives up the most slack when the content track would drop below dimension.content-reading-floor (#242 — shell.css's squeeze, which never widens it and never takes it below panel-floor).

--dimension-room-flank.purpose: a shell geometry input (rail, chrome row, panel clamp, reading floor, device pixel)
--dimension-room-flank.description: The inline room the plugin column takes beside the transcript: the column and the gap between them. The transcript gives it up while the column is in the row, and the composer gives up the same room so both stay on one axis.

--dimension-room-flank-fit.purpose: a shell geometry input (rail, chrome row, panel clamp, reading floor, device pixel)
--dimension-room-flank-fit.description: The room width that seats the plugin column beside the transcript: the reading floor plus the room the column takes (`--dimension-room-flank`). Spelled out, not aliased, so the density copy resolves the gap at the element that reads it.

--dimension-panel-context.purpose: a shell geometry input (rail, chrome row, panel clamp, reading floor, device pixel)
--dimension-panel-context.description: the CONTEXT side-panel track width (§11.1 clamp-overlay). Wider than the list panel on desktop (owner, 2026-08-01: the rpg takeover was "a bit cramped" once the Waystone grew to its focal 120px). SAME 17rem floor — the responsive floor and the mobile full-width sheet are unchanged; only the desktop ideal/max grew (24vw/26rem -> 30vw/30rem). 30vw, not the first-cut 26vw, is the owner ruling (3c49a6cce2): a STANDARD 1280px desktop must reach 384px = the 24rem container step where the Waystone paints at its focal 120px — at 26vw that viewport landed on 20.8rem and got the 96px stone. Early design mocks drew 272/340/416px against the old clamp; this widens the ideal, not the grammar.

--reading-measure.purpose: a reading measure or bubble share
--reading-measure.description: The TRANSCRIPT's LINE-LENGTH cap, expressed in ch so it tracks the font rather than a viewport guess. The transcript had NO cap (`max-width: none`) and measured 98ch at 1280px with panels closed, ~200ch on a 2560 monitor (side-eye aesthetic shakedown, 2026-08-16, #97). Consumed by client globals.css on [data-slot="message-content-column"] as `calc(var(--reading-measure) * var(--appearance-reading-body-scale))`, in a column whose own font-size IS the prose font. It caps the CONTENT COLUMN, not the transcript REGION: --width-shell-content (the user's chatWidthPct dial) still owns how wide the thread runs, so the composer and the row gutters keep their geometry and only the line length is bounded. NOT THE TOP OF THE 65-75 BAND, AND NO LONGER THE APP'S ONE MEASURE (#1145, owner ruling 2026-09-02): 75 CSS ch is 107-117 typographic characters on Geist, so this token is the TRANSCRIPT's deliberate width, not the design law's number. Teaching/body prose takes --reading-measure-prose (47ch), which carries the derivation.

--reading-measure-prose.purpose: a reading measure or bubble share
--reading-measure-prose.description: The TEACHING/BODY-PROSE line-length cap (#1145, owner ruling 2026-09-02) — the app's SECOND reading measure, beside --reading-measure (75ch), which stays the CHAT TRANSCRIPT's and is deliberately not narrowed. DERIVATION (measured, not assumed): CSS ch is the zero-glyph advance = 0.6625em in Geist; the app's own prose averages 0.4248em per glyph at its densest (home's temp-chat gloss) and 0.4629em at its loosest, so 1 CSS ch = 1.43-1.56 typographic characters. 75ch therefore reads 107-117 characters per line — home-surface.ct.tsx measures 117.0 at 1920 — and cannot satisfy the design law's 65-75 band at ANY font size; 47ch = 31.14em = 67.3-73.3 characters, inside the band at both ends. Consumed as max-w-(--reading-measure-prose) on the PARAGRAPH itself, never on a page or on a control block — a ch resolves in the element's own font, so a cap inherited from a wrapper reads at the wrong scale (the #213 and #1130 failure), and a block holding controls keeps the wider measure while the paragraph inside it takes this one. NO -min TWIN: --reading-measure-min is read only by the art-bleed band inset (ui globals.css), the echo bubble box and the hearth hero column — all chat/art geometry, none of them teaching prose — so a prose floor would have no reader; mint one when a prose surface first needs a floor.

--reading-measure-min.purpose: a reading measure or bubble share
--reading-measure-min.description: The FLOOR of the same 65-75ch band (#213). `reading.measure` is a MAX with no MIN, so a docked context panel took 177px straight out of the reading column and the line fell to 59ch — the state a reader who keeps Members open lives in permanently. Consumed by globals.css as `min-width: min(100%, calc(var(--reading-measure-min) * var(--appearance-reading-body-scale)))`: the `min(100%, …)` half is load-bearing, because a pane can be narrower than the floor itself (measured: a 509px CONTENT pane at list+context docked) and a bare min-width would spill the column out of its pane, which is worse than a short line. Holding the floor in THAT state is a shell-grid question (how narrow a panel may push the content pane), not a transcript one — RULED and BUILT at #242 (dimension.content-reading-floor + shell.css's conditional squeeze), for the REAL-CHARACTER floor: that pane is now 579px and holds 65.1 real characters, while this token's 65 ch is still unmet there and stays the stated residual for THAT pane. WHERE IT IS MET IS THE DIAL (#1204, 2026-09-02): 65ch is 650px in Geist (it was 557.7px under the pre-`77e07912eb` fallback stack — the number this paragraph used to quote), and dimension.shell-content-floor is derived from exactly that 650 so the reader's own chat-width dial can no longer be turned below this floor. A docked-panel deficit that outlives both pane floors still can, and that is the residual, stated.

--shadow-prose.value: 0 1px 2px oklch(from var(--color-backdrop) l c h / 0.45), 0 0 6px oklch(from var(--color-backdrop) l c h / 0.25)
--shadow-prose.description: The prose halo over wallpaper (appearance.shadowEffects). Both stops derive from the active backdrop through the relative-colour form so the halo follows the palette's polarity; a frozen black would stay black under a light theme.

--text-shadow-wordmark.description: The wordmark halo over live artwork. Its shadow colour resolves from the active backdrop token.

--shadow-glow.value: 0 0 0 1px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.4), 0 0 18px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.18)
--shadow-glow.description: the ONE rationed accent glow (DESIGN.md §5) — focus/character moment only. It DERIVES from the active theme's --color-primary through the relative-colour form, the same mechanism color.sheen already uses to keep a per-site alpha over a one-decision hue: the old note that per-stop alpha 'must live inside oklch(), so it cannot reference {color.primary}' was a limitation of the plain reference, not of CSS. Why it matters (#232): the glow was the dark Ember literal in EVERY theme, so the Light seed (primary oklch(0.55 0.16 50)) wore the dark ember, and a custom theme's accent never reached its own glow. Relative colour survives Tailwind's build-time inlining of --shadow-* into .shadow-* (probed), so this resolves per theme — including ThemeScope-emitted custom palettes, which no value-set could have covered.

--shadow-layer-ambient-far.description: The deep ambient drop, one layer of the overlay recipe, on its own so a `filter: drop-shadow()` (which takes exactly one layer) carries the same geometry and ingredient. In @theme like every shadow value, so the generated shadow vocabulary stays one list.

--shadow-overlay.description: modal/popover/card elevation (UIP-401) — a LAYERED float recipe (was the single flat 0 24px 80px drop): a 1px edge-light hairline + an inset top-highlight (the light-from-above cue) + a tight contact shadow + the deep ambient drop. All consumers (card/dialog/popover/menu/tooltip/toast/drawer/command-palette/selection-bar/macro-textarea) inherit it via the shadow-overlay utility. Each stop now names a colour INGREDIENT token instead of a literal (#232), so the recipe's GEOMETRY is one decision here and its polarity is the palette's: the four ingredients are the only part a value-set re-values, and a var() ingredient is the only form that survives Tailwind's build-time inlining of --shadow-* into .shadow-*.

--shadow-cta.description: the primary-CTA static top-highlight (a light-from-above catch on the button's top edge) — a subtle inset white-alpha hairline that reads as a raised, tactile primary button. The catch is the `color.shadow-cta-highlight` ingredient token (#232), so a palette can retune it against its own primary. Consumed as `shadow-cta` on buttonVariants intent:primary; the hover state swaps to `shadow-cta-glow` (this highlight + the rationed Ember glow) so the highlight persists under the hover halo.

--shadow-cta-glow.value: inset 0 1px 0 var(--color-shadow-cta-highlight), 0 0 0 1px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.4), 0 0 18px oklch(from var(--color-primary) l c h / 0.18)
--shadow-cta-glow.description: the primary-CTA HOVER treatment — the `shadow.cta` top-highlight PLUS the one rationed Ember glow (the `shadow.glow` stops, inlined so this is a single box-shadow value that keeps BOTH: a `hover:shadow-glow` alone would drop the highlight). Consumed as `hover:shadow-cta-glow` on buttonVariants intent:primary. Both halves DERIVE (#232): the catch from `color.shadow-cta-highlight`, the two glow stops from the active `--color-primary` through the relative-colour form.
